item.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold (Google Threat Intelligence Group)
item.description: Google's threat-intelligence team documents the first attack pipeline it has seen running with no human in the loop: a framework called exploit_agent that watches web software for security patches, compares the code before and after the fix, writes a working exploit for the flaw the patch reveals and launches it. The report also covers open-source AI hacking frameworks used in real intrusions, an influence-operations platform built to run more than 100,000 accounts, and a suspected North Korean group that planted a backdoor by editing Claude Code settings files. First-hand evidence of AI acting as the attacker, and why patched (rather than unknown) flaws become the main target once exploits can be written in hours.

item.title: Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity's /teamwork (Google Research Blog)
item.description: Google's own account of how teams of Gemini 4 agents, each given a narrow slice of context and checked by verifiers like the Lean proof checker and by critic agents, produced a 1.8-million-line machine-checked formalisation of the Weil conjectures across 28,800 subagent calls, plus results in chemistry, algorithms and Rust ports of C++ code. First-hand look at how multi-agent research is actually organised and verified, and what it already delivers.
